name: Example: Finding a Probability Geometrically Using a CDF
problem:
Let the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y$ be $F(x, y),$ where

$$
F(5,5) = 0.9, \quad
F(5,2) = 0.3, \quad
F(0,5) = 0.45, \quad
F(0,2) = 0.15.
$$

Find $P(0 \leq X \leq 5, 2 \leq Y \leq 5).$
worked_solution:
Recall that $F(x,y) = P(X \leq x, Y \leq y)$ is the probability that the pair $(X,Y)$ will lie inside the infinite rectangular region that has its top-right corner at $(x,y)$ and whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes.

Let's sketch the region corresponding to the probability we wish to find.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14274884/assets/181df1b4d320fac30e8fc774975c8e1ae3fa6f4d360a49a38d23f1de96ebf7cc.png)

Geometrically, this region can be obtained as follows:

1\. Take the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at $(5,5).$

2\. Subtract the infinite rectangles that have their top-right corners at $\color{red}(5,2)$ and ${\color{red}{(0,5)}}.$

3\. Finally, we need to *add back* the infinite rectangle that has its top-right corner at ${\color{blue}{(0,2)}}.$ This is because we subtracted this region twice in step 2.

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0\le X\le 5,2\le Y\le 5) & =\overset{\text{top-right corner at [math](5,5)[/math]}}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 5,Y\le 5)}} \\  & \,-\overset{\text{top-right corner at [math](5,2)[/math]}}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 5,Y\le 2)}}-\overset{\text{top-right corner at [math](0,5)[/math]}}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 0,Y\le 5)}} \\  & \,+\overset{\text{top-right corner at [math](0,2)[/math]}}{\overset{⏞}{P(X\le 0,Y\le 2)}} \\  & =F(5,5)-F(5,2)-F(0,5)+F(0,2) \\  & =0.9-0.3-0.45+0.15 \\  & =0.3.\end{aligned}
$$
